parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans presentation, constitutional equality covering gender identity, decriminalised same-sex acts, and functioning courts (Feb 2026 passport relief, 2021 police-sensitisation and conversion-therapy ban) are genuine protections. Against that: documented document/security friction (airport stop despite ID, demanded medical exam), police groping under a 'gender check' pretext, degrading custody in one state, removal of gender-identity sexual-violence safeguards in the new criminal code, and a March 2026 recognition amendment critics call criminalising. Incidents are scattered rather than systemic (official note: abuse 'not systemic'), and no universal-exposure facility rule or organised targeting is documented. Social conservatism (59% disapproval, hostility to Pride) and undated, non-trans-specific violence findings add friction without establishing severity. Worst features are tier 2-3 with partial, demonstrably working recourse: Reduced Risk, but below the 0.65 anchors' steadier protections.
